newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: HOWARD URGES END TO VIOLENCE AS PORT ARTHUR REMEMBERED
The Prime Minister says the greatest memorial to the 35 victims of the Port Arthur massacre a year ago would be a collective national effort to end violence.
Mr Howard says the thoughts of the entire nation are today with those devastated by the tragedy, as they hold a commemorative service to mark the first anniversary of the killings.
He urged Australians to shun violence in the home, against the vulnerable, on the playing field, in the pub, and in any walk of life.
Mr Howard was speaking as chaplins at the Royal Hobart Hospital, were conducting a private service for staff who cared for the wounded.
Earlier, hundreds of people attended a memorial service at the convict church at Port Arthur, which was followed by a period of private mourning.
PRIVATE TRIBUTES FOLLOW PORT ARTHUR SERVICE
The Port Arthur historic site has been closed to the media as families of those killed in the massacre a year ago mourn in private.
Earlier today, up to one thousand people attended a memorial service in the ruins of the convict church.
Many wept during the 30 minute service which finished with an Irish blessing.
On April the 28th, 1996, Martin Bryant opened fire at the Broad Arrow Cafe killing 20 people in about 90 seconds.
In all, 35 people died in his shooting spree.
MOST STATE LEADERS BACK HOWARD'S WIK PLAN
Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge says he'll investigate the possibilities for state legislation to fill the gap in the Commonwealth's plan for native title.
Most state and territory leaders appear to agree with the Prime Minister's 10-point plan to deal with the impasse over native title on pastoral leases, following the High Court's Wik decision.
It's understood Mr Howard has made some concessions from his original plan at talks with the leaders in Canberra.
Mr Borbidge says he still doesn't agree with the outcome, but it's an improvement.
He says his government will consult with industry groups and look at complimentary state legislation to fill the gap that the Commonwealth is unwilling or unable to fill.
AUSTRALIA TO PRESS JAPAN ON GREENHOUSE TARGETS
Australia will push Japan to join in opposition to international targets for cuts in greenhouse gases.
The Prime Minister, John Howard, says he'll raise the climate change issue in talks tonight and tomorrow with Japan's Prime Minister, Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Mr Howard said the proposal for uniform cuts in greenhouse gases posed a significant medium-term economic threat to Australia.
The Federal Government today released studies which estimate that a ten percent cut in carbon dioxide emissions would cost Australia nine-thousand dollars a person.
A 15-percent cut would cost Japan 15-thousand dollars a person.
The study said these costs would be much higher than those for the United States and Europe.
COURT HEARING OVER BONDI MURDER
A Sydney Court has been told that a British tourist was hit by a government bus, while being bashed at Sydney's Bondi Beach late last year.
23-year-old Aaron Martin is facing a committal hearing at Sydney's Downing Central local court, charged with the murder of Brian Hagland.
During his opening address Crown Prosecutor Chris Maxwell QC said Mr Hagland was found lying unconscious on a road at Bondi Beach with shocking injuries to his head and body.
He told the court that during a ferocious attack on the 28-year-old British tourist, Mr Hagland came in contact with a bus turning the corner.
A second man, 23-year-old Sean Cushman, is appearing before the same committal hearing, charged with being an accessory after the fact to murder.
FORMER BOND DIRECTOR GUILTY IN FRAUD CASE
In the Supreme Court in Perth, a former Bond Corporation director Peter Mitchell has admitted his involvement in the nation's biggest case of corporate fraud.
Mitchell had been due to stand trial on charges arising out of the transfer of one Billion dollars from Bell Resources to the Bond group in the late 1980s.
However, Mitchell pleaded guilty instead to charges of failing to use his powers honestly and improper use of his office.
Further charges of conspiracy to defraud were dropped by the prosecution.
Alan Bond pleaded guilty to charges arising out of the fraud last year and is currently serving a four year jail term for the offences.
WOODS TO APPEAR ON FRAUD CHARGES NEXT MONTH
Fraud charges against former Liberal Senator Bob Woods are due to be mentioned in the ACT Magistrates Court next month.
National Party backbencher Michael Cobb is due to face similar charges in early June.
In court today, Magistrate John Burns adjourned both matters, Woods until May the 28th and Cobb until June the 3rd.
Bob Woods is facing 41 counts of defrauding the Commonwealth, while Michael Cobb is facing six counts of defrauding the Commonwealth and five of imposing upon the Commonwealth.
Magistrate Burns also struck out a subpoena from Mr Woods' solicitor requesting documents from Mr Woods former lover Roxanne Cameron be handed over.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
